name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse building and rebuilding your range against a fighter who wants to close it.
instructions: See the opponent starting to shorten the distance.
Score on the way in with your trained lead, then move off line before they set.
Rebuild your range immediately and see the picture clearly again.
Run it again with them entering from the other side.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse taking space and finishing exchanges in position rather than chasing.
instructions: Visualise them giving ground.
See yourself taking space without following them blindly.
Cut their preferred exit, enter behind your trained setup and finish the exchange balanced.
Run it again with them changing direction and adjust instead of chasing.
cue: Take the space, do not chase it.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse waiting for a real committed cue before answering.
instructions: See the opponent step into range.
Read the first committed cue before reacting.
Make the attack miss or fall short, answer with your trained counter, then leave safely.
Run it again with a different entry and wait for the real cue.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse the two or three situations this fight is most likely to be decided in.
instructions: Pick the exchange you expect to repeat most in this fight.
See your entry, your scoring action and your exit in real time.
Run the same situation with the opponent reacting differently.
Finish every repetition balanced and back on guard.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse holding long range with kicks and leaving before the hands arrive.
instructions: See the opponent closing to their punching range.
Meet the entry with your trained long weapon: teep, side kick or lead round kick.
Recover the leg, step off line and rebuild your range before they reset.
Run it again with them slipping under the kick and entering low.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse walking them onto your shots instead of following them around the ring.
instructions: See them giving ground and picking an exit side.
Cut that exit with your feet before you throw.
Enter behind your trained setup and finish with the kick or knee you have drilled.
Run it again with them circling the other way and adjust your cut.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse reading a committed kick or entry and answering it cleanly.
instructions: See the opponent load a kick or step in behind their hands.
Read which one it is before you move.
Check, catch or make it fall short, then answer with your trained return.
Reset your stance and run it again with the other weapon.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse earning the clinch on your terms and scoring before the break.
instructions: See the entry that gets you inside: after their kick, or behind your own hands.
Take your trained grip and win the head or inside position first.
Score with knees or off-balancing before the referee breaks it.
Run it again with them framing and turning out early.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse the main exchanges of this fight across both punching and kicking range.
instructions: Pick the range this fight will mostly be fought at.
See your entry, your scoring action and your exit in real time.
Run the same exchange once with hands and once with legs.
Finish each repetition balanced with both feet under you.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse striking at range while staying honest about the takedown.
instructions: See the opponent closing distance with their hands or a level change.
Decide which it is before you commit your weight.
Score on the entry, then circle off the cage and rebuild your range.
Run it again with the entry becoming a real shot and defend without freezing.
cue: Strike, then get your angle back.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse using the cage to take space rather than chasing in open ground.
instructions: See them backing up and choosing an exit along the fence.
Cut that exit with your feet and put their back to the cage.
Enter behind your trained setup and finish the exchange or take the body lock.
Run it again with them circling out and adjust your angle instead of chasing.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse answering a committed entry without being drawn onto a level change.
instructions: See the opponent commit to an entry.
Read whether the head stays high or drops before you answer.
Counter the high entry with your trained return; meet the low entry with your frame and hips.
Reset your stance and run both versions again.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse getting to your entry and converting the first control position.
instructions: See the strike or feint that sets up your trained entry.
Change levels on your own timing, not theirs, and finish to your control position.
See the first pass or advance you want once you are on top.
Run it again from the cage instead of open space.
cue: Earn the entry, then hold it.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse closing to the clinch and making the cage do the work.
instructions: See your entry into the clinch behind a strike or on their exit.
Take your trained grip and pin them to the cage before you try to score.
Work your knees, elbows or trips from that position without giving up the grip.
Run it again with them turning out and re-clinch instead of chasing.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse moving between striking and grappling on your own decision, not theirs.
instructions: See the striking exchange you want to start with.
Pick the moment you convert it into your trained takedown or clinch entry.
If the entry stalls, see yourself returning to striking rather than forcing it.
Run it again starting from grappling and exiting into strikes.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse the phases this fight is most likely to be decided in.
instructions: Pick the phase you expect to spend most of the fight in: range, clinch or ground.
See your entry into that phase and the first thing you do once you arrive.
See how you get back out if it is not working.
Run it again with the opponent starting the phase instead of you.
cue: Know where you want the fight.

name: Tactical Picture
why: Rehearse the main situation of this fight before the taper takes your sharpness elsewhere.
instructions: Pick the situation you expect to repeat most in this bout.
See your entry, your scoring action and your exit in real time.
Run the same situation again with the opponent reacting differently.
Finish each repetition balanced and ready to continue.

name: Read → React
why: Recognise the moment the opponent commits to closing distance.
instructions: Picture the opponent beginning to close distance.
Notice the first committed step, rhythm change or reach.
Use your trained intercept or exit.
Rebuild your preferred range immediately and repeat with a different entry.
cue: See the step before the shot.

name: Read → React
why: Recognise how the opponent reacts to pressure before committing to the next attack.
instructions: Picture the opponent retreating straight, covering high or planting to counter.
Recognise the reaction before choosing your response.
Use only responses already trained in camp.
Finish each exchange balanced and reset your pressure.

name: Read → React
why: Separate a real committed lead from a feint meant to draw your counter.
instructions: Picture a feint, a half-step and a fully committed lead.
Answer only the committed one; let the other two pass.
Use the counter you have already drilled for that lead.
Reset your guard and read again before anything else.

name: Read → React
why: Rehearse recognising the opponent's action before choosing a response.
instructions: Picture three reactions you expect from this opponent.
See the reaction clearly before you decide what to throw.
Use only responses already trained in camp.
Reset your stance after each exchange and read again.

name: Read → React
why: Recognise the entry early enough to use your longest weapon.
instructions: Picture the opponent stepping in, switching stance or loading a kick.
Identify which one it is before you commit.
Answer with your trained teep, check or lateral exit.
Rebuild your range and repeat with a different entry.

name: Read → React
why: Recognise how the opponent answers pressure before you commit to the next attack.
instructions: Picture them retreating straight, checking your kicks or planting to fire back.
See the reaction before choosing your response.
Use only the entries and finishes trained in camp.
Reset your stance and read again after each exchange.

name: Read → React
why: Tell a committed kick from a feint before you counter.
instructions: Picture a hand feint, a low kick and a committed head kick.
Answer only the committed weapon; let the feints pass.
Use the check or catch you have drilled, then your trained return.
Reset and read again without leaning forward.

name: Read → React
why: Recognise the moment the clinch is available and the moment it is gone.
instructions: Picture them catching a kick, framing you off, or leaning in after a combination.
See which of those actually offers you the clinch.
Take your trained grip only on the real opening.
When the grip is denied, break cleanly and reset rather than wrestling for it.

name: Read → React
why: Rehearse recognising hand or leg attacks early enough to answer them.
instructions: Picture three familiar attacks from this opponent, at least one with the legs.
Recognise which weapon is coming before you move.
Answer with the block, check or exit already trained in camp.
Reset your stance and read again.

name: Read → React
why: Separate a striking entry from a takedown entry before you commit.
instructions: Picture the opponent stepping in with hands high, then stepping in with a level change.
Read the head position before you choose.
Strike and angle off the high entry; frame and sprawl on the low one.
Rebuild your range and repeat with the two mixed.
cue: Watch the level, not the hands.

name: Read → React
why: Recognise how the opponent escapes your pressure at the cage.
instructions: Picture them circling out, framing off, or shooting to escape the fence.
See which escape they choose before you commit your next attack.
Answer with the trained cut, the trained frame-break or the trained sprawl.
Re-establish the fence and read again.
cue: See the escape before it happens.

name: Read → React
why: Answer only genuine commitment, in striking and in grappling.
instructions: Picture a feint, a real punch entry and a real shot.
Let the feint go; answer the punch with your trained counter.
Meet the shot with hips and frames, not with a punch.
Reset your stance and read again.

name: Read → React
why: Recognise which takedown entry the opponent's stance is actually giving you.
instructions: Picture them square, bladed, and backing toward the cage.
See which of your trained entries each stance opens.
Enter on the one that is available rather than the one you prefer.
Reset to your stance and read the position again.
cue: Take the entry they give you.

name: Read → React
why: Recognise how the opponent defends the clinch so you pick the right grip.
instructions: Picture them framing on your hips, underhooking, or turning to face you.
See which defence appears before you choose your grip.
Use the trained answer to that defence and keep them on the cage.
If you lose the grip, reset your posture and re-enter.

name: Read → React
why: Recognise which phase the opponent is offering and take it deliberately.
instructions: Picture them striking at range, then backing to the cage, then reaching for the clinch.
Name the phase each one offers before you act.
Take the phase you are better in, using a trained entry.
Reset to your stance and read the next one.

name: Read → React
why: Rehearse reading strike or grappling intent before responding.
instructions: Picture three familiar actions from this opponent, at least one a level change.
Recognise which it is before you move.
Use only the response already trained in camp.
Reset your stance and read again.

name: Read → React
why: Rehearse recognising the opponent's action before choosing a response.
instructions: Picture three familiar actions from this opponent.
See the action clearly before you decide what to do.
Use only responses already trained in camp.
Reset your position after each exchange and read again.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse recovering range after it has been taken from you.
instructions: Picture your back finding the ropes with the opponent in your chest.
Do not trade to escape. Exhale, frame, and pivot off the ropes.
Rebuild your range and restart your jab from the centre.
Then picture them timing your exit. Change the exit side and continue working.
cue: Get your feet back, then your range.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse restarting pressure from position after being caught or escaped.
instructions: Picture getting caught while entering.
Do not rush back in. Exhale, rebuild your stance and restart your pressure from position.
Then picture the opponent escaping your trap.
Reset the angle instead of chasing.
cue: Reset the angle, not the pace.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse staying patient after a counter is read and beaten.
instructions: Picture your counter being anticipated and answered.
Do not start hunting. Exhale, rebuild your guard and re-establish distance.
Then picture the opponent refusing to lead at all.
Give them one trained lead of your own to react to, and go back to reading.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse recovering composure and position after a bad moment.
instructions: Picture being caught clean in an exchange.
Exhale, cover, move your feet and rebuild your stance.
Then picture your best shot being blocked twice in a row.
Change the setup rather than the intensity and continue working.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse recovering after your long weapons are caught or walked through.
instructions: Picture your kick being caught and your balance taken.
Recover your leg, post your stance and step out to a new angle.
Then picture them walking through your teep into punching range.
Frame, pivot off, and rebuild your range before you throw again.
cue: Recover the leg, then the range.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse restarting pressure after being checked or countered on the way in.
instructions: Picture your entry meeting a hard check or a clean counter.
Do not rush the next entry. Exhale, reset your stance and re-enter behind a setup.
Then picture them circling out of your trap.
Cut the new exit instead of chasing the old one.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse staying composed when your reads stop paying.
instructions: Picture countering late and taking the shot instead.
Exhale, cover, check, and re-establish your distance.
Then picture an opponent who will not commit to anything.
Offer one trained lead to draw a reaction, then return to reading.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse losing the clinch without losing the round.
instructions: Picture your grip being stripped and being turned out of the clinch.
Do not reach after it. Recover your posture and re-establish striking range.
Then picture being kneed on the way in.
Reset your entry, change the level of your grip and work again.
cue: Lose the grip, keep the position.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse recovering composure and stance after adversity.
instructions: Picture being caught clean or having a kick checked hard.
Exhale, cover, move your feet and rebuild your stance.
Then picture your main weapon being read twice.
Change the setup rather than the intensity and continue working.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse getting back to open space after being taken out of it.
instructions: Picture your back hitting the cage with the opponent tied up on you.
Frame, get your hips out and circle back to open space.
Then picture being taken down cleanly.
Protect first, build your frames, get back to your feet and rebuild your range.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse restarting pressure after it is broken or reversed.
instructions: Picture them escaping the fence and turning you into it.
Do not panic-swing. Frame, circle out and re-establish your forward position.
Then picture being caught coming in.
Exhale, reset your stance and re-enter behind a setup rather than a rush.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse composure when your counter is baited into a takedown.
instructions: Picture your counter drawing a level change and ending on the mat.
Protect, frame, build your base and return to your feet.
Then picture them refusing to lead while the clock runs.
Give one trained lead to create the read, then go back to waiting.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse continuing to work after a defended entry or a lost position.
instructions: Picture your first takedown being defended.
Stay composed. Recover position, reconnect to your next control option and continue working.
Then picture losing a dominant position.
Protect first, rebuild position and return to your next task.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse recovering when the clinch is reversed against you.
instructions: Picture being turned and pinned to the cage yourself.
Frame, get your hips free and switch to your trained escape grip.
Then picture your entry being sprawled on.
Recover your posture, return to your feet and re-enter behind a strike.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse being forced into your weaker phase and getting back out.
instructions: Picture the fight dragged into the phase you least want.
Stay composed, survive the first thirty seconds and work your trained exit.
Return to the phase you chose and restart from there.
Then run it once more where you stay and solve it instead of leaving.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse recovering composure and position after a bad moment.
instructions: Picture being caught clean or taken down.
Protect first, then build your frames and your base.
Recover position, reconnect to your next task and continue working.
Then run it again from a different bad position and finish the same way.

name: Pressure → Reset
why: Rehearse adversity that ends with a decision, not with dwelling.
instructions: Picture the moment in this fight that would rattle you most.
Exhale, protect, and rebuild your position.
Reconnect to your next useful task and continue working.
Run it once more and finish it the same way.

name: Familiar & Ready
why: Make tomorrow familiar without adding new information.
instructions: Picture arriving, wrapping up and warming up.
Hear the room and your corner.
Feel yourself getting sharper as the warm-up progresses.
See the opening bell and settle into your normal stance.
Use the same cue you have trusted in camp, then leave it there.

name: Familiar & Ready
why: Make tomorrow familiar without adding new information.
instructions: Picture arriving, wrapping up, shins and pads on, and warming up.
Hear the room and your corner.
Feel yourself getting sharper as the warm-up progresses.
See the opening bell, settle into your normal stance and take the first look.
Use the same cue you have trusted in camp, then leave it there.

name: Familiar & Ready
why: Make tomorrow familiar without adding new information.
instructions: Picture arriving, wrapping up, gloves on and warming up.
Hear the room and your corner.
See yourself walking to the cage and stepping through the door.
Settle into your normal stance and take the first look at the opening range.
Use the same cue you have trusted in camp, then leave it there.

name: Familiar & Ready
why: Make tomorrow familiar without adding new information.
instructions: Picture arriving, getting ready and warming up in your normal order.
Hear the room and your corner.
See the start of the bout and settle into your normal position.
Use the same cue you have trusted in camp, then leave it there.

name: Trust → Compete
why: Stop conscious over-analysis and hand the fight to your trained reactions.
instructions: See the ring and feel your feet underneath you.
See the opponent clearly. One breath.
Bring up your fight cue.
Read what is actually there and trust your reactions.
pre_bout: Twenty seconds: one breath, feet under you, fight cue up, go.

name: Trust → Compete
why: Stop conscious over-analysis and hand the fight to your trained reactions.
instructions: See the ring and feel your feet and shins loose.
See the opponent clearly. One breath.
Bring up your fight cue.
Read what is actually there and trust your reactions.
pre_bout: Twenty seconds: one breath, feet under you, fight cue up, go.

name: Trust → Compete
why: Stop conscious over-analysis and hand the fight to your trained reactions.
instructions: See the cage and feel your feet underneath you.
Feel the gloves and see the opponent clearly. One breath.
Bring up your fight cue.
Read the opening range and trust your reactions.
pre_bout: Twenty seconds: one breath, feet under you, fight cue up, go.

name: Trust → Compete
why: Stop conscious over-analysis and hand the bout to your trained reactions.
instructions: See the competition area and feel your feet underneath you.
See the opponent clearly. One breath.
Bring up your trusted cue.
Read what is actually there and trust your reactions.
pre_bout: Twenty seconds: one breath, feet under you, cue up, go.
